BN4.SI remains a SELL. Despite a run of corporate activity — a S$400M perpetual securities redemption, the ~S$1.2B Greater Tokyo data centre acquisition via Keppel DC REIT, and a SAF plant joint venture on Jurong Island — none of these moves closes the valuation gap that makes Underweight versus the Straits Times Index the only defensible stance. At a spot price of S$11.13, the stock trades at a -6.2% discount to our blended intrinsic value of S$10.44, and our 12-month price target of S$10.89 implies a total shareholder return of just +0.9% (capital loss of -2.2% offset by a +3.1% dividend yield) — an -801 basis-point shortfall to the STI's expected +8.9% return. The corporate actions modestly improve the structural narrative; they do not alter the verdict.

The multiple itself is the problem. A 39.1x P/E and 26.1x EV/EBITDA price in execution that leaves no room for error, yet the underlying capital efficiency — a negative FCF yield of -0.36% and an ROIC of only 2.2% against a WACC of 10.2% — is firmly conglomerate-grade rather than growth-stock-grade. Our DCF base intrinsic value of S$7.87 and bear intrinsic value of S$9.62 both sit materially below spot; even the scenario EV of S$10.67 implies -4.1% from current levels. The Power Law score of 4/10 and VGPM Value grade of C reinforce what the numbers already say: the market is paying a premium it has not yet been offered a reason to collect, which is precisely the dynamic our TRAP RISK HIGH indicator is designed to flag.

We share Phillip Securities Research's view (Paul Chew, 12 August 2025, BUY) that the M1-Simba disposal failure is a one-time drag rather than a structural impairment, and the asset-light flywheel is genuinely compelling: funds under management reached S$106B in July 2026 against a S$100B end-2026 consensus target, while recurring income in H1 2026 rose 13% year-on-year to S$467M. The Apollo US$1.5B Offshore Fund commitment in July 2026 validates the capital-light model, and if FUM reaches S$120B or beyond by year-end — as our research digest projects — fee income could re-rate the multiple meaningfully. That is the key upside risk to our SELL, and we state it plainly. Where we part ways with the street is on valuation: Phillip's own SOTP-derived target of S$10.7 sits below the current spot of S$11.13, and our 12-month price target of S$10.89 offers only marginal upside against a benchmark that should return nearly nine percent — marginal upside is not enough.

Our price target of S$10.89 is derived from a blended scenario framework: the DCF base intrinsic value of S$7.87 is weighted at 40%, the DCF bear intrinsic value of S$9.62 at 20%, the DCF bull intrinsic value of S$16.74 at 15%, and the scenario EV of S$10.67 at 25%, all discounted at a WACC of 10.2%, producing a blended output of S$10.44 that is then adjusted upward by 4.3% for near-term FUM momentum to arrive at S$10.89. The prevailing macro regime — risk-off, medium volatility, recession risk low, but consumer sentiment in distress territory and imminent Fed rate-hike expectations dominant despite healthy labour markets — imposes a conviction cap that tilts against re-rating conglomerate multiples in the near term. That regime reinforces rather than contradicts our Underweight stance, and we maintain it.

BN4.SI.rationale:
BN4.SI remains a SELL. Despite a run of corporate activity — a S$400M perpetual securities redemption, the ~S$1.2B Greater Tokyo data centre acquisition via Keppel DC REIT, and a SAF plant joint venture on Jurong Island — none of these moves closes the valuation gap that makes Underweight versus the Straits Times Index the only defensible stance. At a spot price of S$11.13, the stock trades at a -6.2% discount to our blended intrinsic value of S$10.44, and our 12-month price target of S$10.89 implies a total shareholder return of just +0.9% (capital loss of -2.2% offset by a +3.1% dividend yield) — an -801 basis-point shortfall to the STI's expected +8.9% return. The corporate actions modestly improve the structural narrative; they do not alter the verdict.

The multiple itself is the problem. A 39.1x P/E and 26.1x EV/EBITDA price in execution that leaves no room for error, yet the underlying capital efficiency — a negative FCF yield of -0.36% and an ROIC of only 2.2% against a WACC of 10.2% — is firmly conglomerate-grade rather than growth-stock-grade. Our DCF base intrinsic value of S$7.87 and bear intrinsic value of S$9.62 both sit materially below spot; even the scenario EV of S$10.67 implies -4.1% from current levels. The Power Law score of 4/10 and VGPM Value grade of C reinforce what the numbers already say: the market is paying a premium it has not yet been offered a reason to collect, which is precisely the dynamic our TRAP RISK HIGH indicator is designed to flag.

We share Phillip Securities Research's view (Paul Chew, 12 August 2025, BUY) that the M1-Simba disposal failure is a one-time drag rather than a structural impairment, and the asset-light flywheel is genuinely compelling: funds under management reached S$106B in July 2026 against a S$100B end-2026 consensus target, while recurring income in H1 2026 rose 13% year-on-year to S$467M. The Apollo US$1.5B Offshore Fund commitment in July 2026 validates the capital-light model, and if FUM reaches S$120B or beyond by year-end — as our research digest projects — fee income could re-rate the multiple meaningfully. That is the key upside risk to our SELL, and we state it plainly. Where we part ways with the street is on valuation: Phillip's own SOTP-derived target of S$10.7 sits below the current spot of S$11.13, and our 12-month price target of S$10.89 offers only marginal upside against a benchmark that should return nearly nine percent — marginal upside is not enough.

Our price target of S$10.89 is derived from a blended scenario framework: the DCF base intrinsic value of S$7.87 is weighted at 40%, the DCF bear intrinsic value of S$9.62 at 20%, the DCF bull intrinsic value of S$16.74 at 15%, and the scenario EV of S$10.67 at 25%, all discounted at a WACC of 10.2%, producing a blended output of S$10.44 that is then adjusted upward by 4.3% for near-term FUM momentum to arrive at S$10.89. The prevailing macro regime — risk-off, medium volatility, recession risk low, but consumer sentiment in distress territory and imminent Fed rate-hike expectations dominant despite healthy labour markets — imposes a conviction cap that tilts against re-rating conglomerate multiples in the near term. That regime reinforces rather than contradicts our Underweight stance, and we maintain it.
